items.description: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows and flow modules, simplifying how you build, test, and deploy customer experience flows while minimizing impact to live end-customer traffic. With this launch, you can now create immutable versions of a flow and attach one or more friendly names (i.e., aliases) to a version, then point resources such as queues, quick connects, and phone numbers at an alias instead of a specific version. Rolling out a new version takes a single update, with no need to republish or relink each resource. For example, you can publish an updated customer experience flow as a new version and validate it in a test environment while live traffic stays on the current version, then repoint the production alias to move every phone number to the new version in a single update. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see Flow versioning and aliasing in the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics
items.description: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch . The integration collects Kafka exporter metrics and consumer-group lag metrics from your Amazon MSK clusters. Managed Prometheus collectors discover and collect Prometheus metrics from your workloads, so you don't run and operate collection agents yourself. You ingest the collected metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace or into Amazon CloudWatch, where you query and analyze them. You monitor Kafka stream health and consumer performance with consumer-group metrics. This helps you detect processing bottlenecks in your streaming applications. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where managed Prometheus collectors are generally available. To learn more, see the documentation for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch .

items.title: Amazon Quick Introduces Quick Essentials
items.description: Amazon Quick introduces Quick Essentials for enterprises. The plan makes it easier for organizations to get started with all the features of Quick such as AI-powered chat, Research, Flows, and Apps, and lets users view and interact with Quick Sight dashboards and reports and then manage adoption at the desired pace. In AWS Regions where Amazon Quick is available, Quick Sight Reader users are upgraded to Quick Essentials at no additional per-user cost. With Quick Essentials, Quick Sight Readers can ask their dashboards questions in plain language, like what drove a revenue dip in March, and dig into the details with follow-up questions. They can turn the answer into a document, presentation, or spreadsheet for their team. When they need more context, Research pulls from their data, files, and the web into a detailed report with citations. If they need the same update every week, Flows can build it and send it automatically. When they need a tool that doesn't exist yet, like a request tracker, they can describe it and Apps builds it, without writing code. Existing dashboards, Favorites, and Recents stay in place. Row-level and column-level security apply to every answer, and data is not shared across customers or used to train shared models. Administrators continue to manage the capabilities with custom permission profiles that can be applied to any user or a role. Quick Essentials is enabled in a phased rollout across AWS Regions where Quick AI features are available . To learn more, read the Amazon Quick Community blog post . For pricing details, visit the Amazon Quick pricing page .

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints
items.description: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning, enabling you to run several models on a single GPU instead of dedicating a whole accelerator to each one. Using NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, SageMaker AI divides a GPU into as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers serving small and mid-size models, such as fine-tuned variants, embedding models, rerankers, and classifiers, previously had to give every model an entire accelerator, so an instance hosted no more models than it had GPUs and paid for GPU capacity those models could never use. With GPU partitioning, you choose how to divide the GPUs behind your endpoint and place each model on a partition sized to fit it. Several models then share one accelerator with hardware-enforced isolation, so a busy model cannot take memory or throughput from the models beside it. Right-sizing an accelerator to a workload also opens up newer instance generations that would otherwise be more capacity than a single model needs. You configure GPU partitioning when you create an endpoint that hosts inference components, and you continue to invoke each model by name, so your application code doesn't change. GPU partitioning is available on P4d, P5, G7, and G7e instances in US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (Ireland). To learn more, visit the Amazon SageMaker AI deployment page and see the Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide .

items.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg table optimization in the US West (N. California) Region
items.description: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports automatic table optimization for Apache Iceberg tables in the US West (N. California) Region. Apache Iceberg is an open table format that delivers fast query performance over large tables in data lakes. With this launch, you can enable table optimization for individual tables or for all tables in your Data Catalog. Apache Iceberg tables accumulate small files, snapshots, and unreferenced files with every write, which slows queries and increases storage costs over time. Table optimization continuously monitors your tables to compact small files in the background, remove snapshots that are past your retention settings, and delete unreferenced files that are no longer needed. You can monitor each run from the AWS Glue console, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and logs. You can enable table optimization using the AWS Glue console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. For the full list of Regions where table optimization is available, see Supported Regions for table optimizers . To learn more, see Optimizing Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue Developer Guide. To get started, visit the AWS Glue product page .

items.title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts
items.description: Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers - eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account. From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. Partners can revoke a subsidiary authorization or a subsidiary connection at any time, which immediately stops that subsidiary from creating new offers - agreements and offers already extended to buyers remain unchanged. This capability is available today at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, see   Managing subsidiary account connections  and   Creating private offers as a subsidiary account  .

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle and SQL Server now support storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes
items.description: Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Amazon RDS for Oracle now support RDS storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes . RDS storage autoscaling automatically scales storage capacity in response to growing database workloads, with zero downtime. Additional storage volumes allow you to add up to three additional volumes to increase your storage capacity up to 256 TiB. Previously, you had to manually provision storage capacity on the additional storage volumes based on anticipated application capacity demands while autoscaling could be enabled on the primary storage volume. Under-provisioning could result in application downtime, and over-provisioning could result in under-utilized resources and higher costs. With RDS storage autoscaling, you simply set your desired maximum storage limit for each additional storage volume, and autoscaling takes care of the rest. RDS storage autoscaling continuously monitors actual storage consumption, and scales capacity up automatically when actual utilization approaches provisioned storage capacity. Autoscaling works with new and existing database instances. Autoscaling has no additional charges and you only pay for the provisioned storage resources. You can enable it by using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or Amazon RDS API. RDS storage autoscaling for additional storage volumes is available for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Amazon RDS for Oracle in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, please visit the Amazon RDS storage autoscaling documentation.

items.title: Amazon Aurora now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange
items.description: Starting today, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition  introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can select cryptographic groups from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our getting started page .

items.title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports updating connector plugins and worker configurations
items.description: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now lets you update the custom plugin and worker configuration of an existing connector. This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, updating a connector's plugin or worker configuration meant deleting the connector and recreating it - a disruptive operation that added risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can update a connector's plugin and worker configuration in place. The connector keeps its committed offsets, so its tasks continue processing from where they left off once the update completes. This capability is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is supported. To learn more, visit Amazon MSK Connect developer guide .

items.title: AWS Step Functions workflows now available as AI agent tools
items.description: You can now use your AWS Step Functions workflows as tools for AI agents through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. Your agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. Agents can use your existing Standard and Express workflows as tools. AWS Step Functions is a visual workflow service capable of orchestrating over 220 AWS services to help customers build distributed applications at scale. AgentCore Gateway connects AI agents to tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). With this launch, your agents can run multi-step business processes in the same order every time. For example, a customer support agent can start your refund workflow, and Step Functions runs the eligibility check, manager approval, and credit steps, so every refund follows your policy. Agents can also look up workflow runs, so an operations agent can tell your on-call engineer which order runs failed overnight and where, letting them go straight to fixing the step that broke. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway is available. You pay standard rates for Step Functions and AgentCore Gateway. To get started, follow the tutorial in the Step Functions Developer Guide. For all supported operations and setup options, see Step Functions connector targets in the AgentCore Gateway documentation . If you build with an AI coding assistant such as Kiro, the Agent Toolkit for AWS gives it skills and guidance for building on AWS.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
items.description: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in two additional AWS Regions: Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town). DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to ten times performance improvement, from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second. With DAX, you can accelerate read-intensive and bursty workloads such as real-time bidding, gaming leaderboards, and retail product catalogs, while offloading read traffic from your DynamoDB tables. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so you can add microsecond-latency caching to your applications with minimal code changes. Customers can now keep cached data within the Region and meet low-latency requirements while benefiting from a fully managed service, including automated patching and failover. To learn more, see the Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator page . For the full list of Regions where DAX is available, see the AWS Regional Services page .

items.title: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade to Grafana version 13.2
items.description: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade from Grafana version 12.4 to 13.2. Upgrading to version 13.2 brings features launched as part of open-source Grafana versions 13.0 to 13.2. These include Git Sync for dashboards, dynamic dashboards, and PromQL query support in the Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin. With Git Sync, you can treat dashboards as code by linking a workspace to a Git repository. Dashboard modifications can be tracked, reviewed, and reverted through version control. Dynamic dashboards bring a more adaptable approach to layout and paneling. You can construct responsive views driven by conditions that respond to the data and variables in scope. With Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin support for Prometheus Query Language, you can use PromQL to query metrics that CloudWatch takes in via its OpenTelemetry (OTLP) endpoint, in addition to the existing Metric Search and Metrics Insights query types. In-place upgrade to Grafana 13.2 is supported in all AWS regions where Amazon Managed Grafana is generally available. You can upgrade with just a few clicks from the AWS Console, AWS SDK or AWS CLI. For a complete list of new features, refer to Differences between Grafana versions in the Amazon Managed Grafana User Guide. For upgrade instructions, see Update your workspace version . To learn more about Amazon Managed Grafana features and its pricing, visit the product page and pricing page .

items.title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
items.description: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP as source or destination locations. You can now run Windows to Windows transfers, such as from an on-premises file server to FSx for Windows File Server. Additionally, Enhanced mode agents can now run on Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization version 4.20 or later. With this launch, you can use the same location options in Enhanced mode as in Basic mode. Enhanced mode processes data in parallel for higher performance, removes file count limitations, and provides detailed data transfer metrics. OpenShift Virtualization expands your agent deployment options alongside VMware ESXi, KVM, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Amazon EC2. You can get started by choosing Enhanced mode when you create a task in the AWS DataSync console . These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS DataSync documentation .
products: Amazon Fsx For Windows File Server

items.title: ACM now supports ACME for public certificates in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.description: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) ACME protocol support is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West), providing a fully managed ACME server endpoint that issues public TLS certificates from Amazon Trust Services using any ACMEv2-compatible client, including Certbot, cert-manager for Kubernetes, and acme.sh. With the CA/Browser Forum mandating 47-day certificate lifetimes by 2029, manual management of public certificates becomes untenable. ACME support in ACM gives developers a standards-based path to fully automate certificate issuance and renewal. To learn more, visit the AWS News blog post , the ACM ACME documentation , the ACM pricing page , and the AWS Regional Services page .

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports SOCI-indexed images to start training jobs in seconds
items.description: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces support for Seekable OCI (SOCI)-indexed container images for training and processing jobs, so your jobs start running your code sooner. SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, cutting GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90%, with no impact on training performance. Before a training or processing job can run, SageMaker AI downloads its container image to the instance. For deep learning images, which routinely exceed 10 GB, that download adds minutes to the start of every job, and you pay for that time. Now, when your image includes a SOCI index, SageMaker AI lazy-loads the image, fetching only the files needed to start the container and streaming the rest in the background as your code runs. To use this feature, reference a SOCI-indexed image from a private Amazon ECR repository in your training or processing job. You can use a pre-indexed AWS Deep Learning Container by changing the image tag to its -soci variant, or add a SOCI index to your own image in Amazon ECR with open-source tools, without rebuilding the image. No changes to your job definition, entry point, or data channels are needed. SageMaker AI checks for an index automatically and images without an index download as before. If an index can't be used, the job falls back to a standard download and continues running. SOCI-indexed images for SageMaker AI training and processing jobs are available today in all AWS Regions where SageMaker AI is available, through the SageMaker AI APIs, CLIs, SDKs, and Console. To learn more, see the documentation for training jobs and processing jobs , or read the launch blog .

items.title: Amazon Redshift announces hands-off automated cross-region backups
items.description: Amazon Redshift announces automated cross-region snapshot copy for Amazon Redshift. You can now have your Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup automatically backed up to the target AWS region(s) you choose. The automated cross-region snapshot copy feature will automatically, always copy the most recent snapshot with no manual intervention, continuously and incrementally and ensure your cluster is backed-up to the destination region(s), giving you additional options for business continuity. The benefit to enabling the new automated cross-region snapshot copy feature is that you do not need to manually intervene to initiate a cross-region snapshot copy when an unplanned outage event occurs. Also, this feature takes the most recent snapshot available on your system to copy to the destination region, so you don't have to wait for the next snapshot to be taken, making it independent of your snapshot schedule on your local cluster. To configure cross-region snapshot copy, you need to enable the automated cross-region snapshot copy feature for each cluster and configure the destination region(s) to copy snapshots and how long to keep copied automated snapshots in the destination Region. You can choose the retention period for automated snapshots in the destination region. User snapshots are retained until you explicitly delete them. To restore the snapshot in the destination region, use the snapshot restore feature to a new provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup. Snapshots copied with the automated cross-region snapshot copy feature have names prefixed with `copy` in the destination region. This feature is available in all regions AWS Commercial and GovCloud (US) regions. For more details on configuration and usage see the Amazon Redshift documentation sections for cross-region snapshot copy: Amazon Redshift snapshots and backups . For details on restoring a cluster from a snapshot, see the documentation for Restoring a cluster from a snapshot . For pricing information, please review the 'Backup and storage' and 'Data transfer' sections of the Amazon Redshift pricing page .

items.title: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management and cross-account backup in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
items.description: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management, cross-account backup, and delegated administrators in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. These capabilities help you centrally manage, monitor, and copy backups across the accounts in your organization using AWS Organizations. With cross-account management, you can deploy organization-wide backup policies from your AWS Organizations management account or a delegated administrator account. You can also monitor backup, copy, and restore jobs across all of your organization accounts from one place. With cross-account backup, you can copy recovery points to a backup vault in another account in your organization, which adds protection against accidental or malicious deletion in the source account. You can also register a member account as a delegated administrator, so your teams can manage backups across your organization without needing access to your management account. There is no additional charge to use these capabilities; standard AWS Backup pricing applies. To learn more, see the AWS Backup documentation at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/ . To get started, visit the AWS Backup console at https://console.aws.amazon.com/backup .

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations
items.description: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations, named permission sets that control what actions individual project members can perform. Previously, project members could only be assigned Owner or Contributor designations, which provided nearly identical permissions. With custom designations, administrators define permission sets that align with their organization's personas and assign them to project members. Designations govern all actions within a project, providing administrators with a single permission model for separation of duties. Administrators create designations in the SageMaker Unified Studio administration portal by selecting permissions grouped into categories such as Catalog, Subscriptions, Connections, Notebooks, and Data Agent. For example, a "Data Steward" designation might include permissions to approve subscription requests and publish assets, while an "Analyst" designation is limited to querying data and running notebooks. Each designation is defined at the domain level and assigned across any project in that domain. When a member performs an action, SageMaker Unified Studio evaluates their assigned designation and permits or denies the request. Data engineers, stewards, analysts, and automated pipelines can now work within the same project with differentiated access, removing the need to create separate projects to isolate permissions. Every domain includes two managed designations, Owner and Contributor, and administrators can create up to 10 additional designations. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, visit the Designations documentation.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch
items.description: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports the September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch (MRP) for Oracle Database version 19c and 26ai. An MRP is a minor engine version that builds on a quarterly Release Update (RU), bundling Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update (CSPU) with additional Oracle-recommended fixes. The September 2026 MRP is applied on top of the July 2026 RU and includes the Oracle September CSPU . We recommend upgrading to the September 2026 MRP as it includes the latest security updates for Oracle Database. This release also includes the updated Oracle time zone file (DST version 46), which reflects the latest daylight saving time rule changes in several regions, including British Columbia and Alberta in Canada (effective November 1, 2026) and Morocco and Western Sahara (effective September 20, 2026), which are moving to permanent UTC offsets. If you store timestamps that include time zone information for these areas, the updated time zone file keeps that data aligned with the new rules. You can apply the September 2026 MRP for new database instances, or upgrade existing instances to engine version 19.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-09.r2 or 26.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-09.r2 from the Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. To learn more about Oracle MRPs supported on Amazon RDS for each engine version, see the Amazon RDS for Oracle Release notes .

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 is now available
items.description: AWS announces the general availability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 (@aws/agentcore 1.0.0), rebuilt with faster startup, a consistent command structure, and support for more AgentCore resources. The CLI helps developers create, develop, deploy, and operate AI agents and supporting resources from the terminal. With version 1.0, developers can use the project workflow or work directly with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments without first adding them to a project. Developers can invoke existing resources by ID or ARN, open an interactive shell, export a harness, and use searchable menus, resource pickers, and guided workflows. Consistent global flags provide region selection, JSON output, debugging, and version information across commands. Existing projects can be migrated to AgentCore version 1 using the agentcore migrate command. Install AgentCore CLI version 1.0 from npm or explore the source on GitHub . To learn more, visit the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page , AgentCore CLI reference , and Get started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore .

items.title: Public endpoints for Amazon ElastiCache Serverless now in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.description: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports public endpoints in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. A public endpoint lets you connect to your cache from a serverless function or any application running outside a VPC, without setting up a VPN, a bastion host, or an SSH tunnel. With a public endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless gives you a fully managed cache with no VPC to configure and no infrastructure to provision, and you can create one in under a minute. Every connection uses IAM authentication over TLS 1.3, so there's no password to store or rotate. Connect using Valkey GLIDE 2.2 or later, which has built-in IAM support, or another Valkey client paired with the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache, an open-source library that generates and refreshes IAM authentication tokens for you. With this expansion, public endpoints for ElastiCache Serverless are now available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for using public endpoints beyond standard ElastiCache Serverless pricing. To get started, create a Valkey 9.0 or later serverless cache with a public endpoint using the AWS Management Console, AWS SDK, or AWS CLI. To learn more about public endpoints, see Create a Valkey serverless cache with a public endpoint .

items.title: AWS Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading for Lambda Managed Instances
items.description: AWS Lambda now supports Seekable OCI (SOCI)  for lazy loading Event Functions packaged as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images running on Lambda Managed Instances . With SOCI support, Lambda fetches only the files needed at each stage of the execution environment startup rather than downloading the entire image upfront, reducing container startup times by up to 70%. Customers building compute-intensive applications such as data processing pipelines, high-throughput API backends, and batch computation workloads require substantial memory and CPU resources to process large datasets, serve low-latency responses at scale, and run complex computations efficiently. Container images for these workloads can reach several gigabytes, and downloading and preparing the full image can take several minutes when provisioning new execution environments. SOCI support on Lambda Managed Instances eliminates this bottleneck by streaming only the required files at each stage of the execution environment startup, so your functions start faster as you scale. To get started, create a SOCI index  (a table of contents for the files in your image layers) for your container image and push it to Amazon ECR . When creating or updating your function, set the image URI to the SOCI-indexed tag in Amazon ECR (for example, my-function:v1-soci) and publish a function version. Lambda automatically detects the SOCI index and enables lazy loading with no additional configuration. If you use a coding assistant such as Kiro, Claude Code, or Codex, install the Lambda Managed Instances skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS to configure and deploy functions through your agent. The feature is available in all AWS commercial Regions where Lambda Managed Instances is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda Managed Instances developer guide .

items.title: Introducing time series collections for the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
items.description: Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection. Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage.  With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. Alerting and anomaly detection are also now available, so customers can get notified about issues and spot unusual patterns in their log and event data without separate tooling. Time series collections are available today in all AWS Regions where OpenSearch Serverless is available. To learn more about the pricing for the new warm storage,  see OpenSearch Serverless pricing . To learn more about time series collections on Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, see the OpenSearch Serverless feature page , the launch blog , and the AWS documentation .

items.title: Quick now supports smart approvals for agentic actions
items.description: Amazon Quick now supports smart approvals, a review layer that reduces unnecessary approval prompts while preserving human oversight of the actions that matter most. As agents take more actions on a user's behalf, such as sending email, updating records, and creating tickets, asking a person to approve every step leads to approval fatigue and weaker oversight over time. With smart approvals, a separate review model called the classifier evaluates each eligible action against the user's request. It approves routine actions automatically and refers consequential actions to the user for review. Your existing policies always come first. Smart approvals only reviews actions where the user's setting is "ask" each time. Denied actions stay denied, and smart approvals never grants new access. The classifier sends higher-impact actions to the user for review. These include sending content outside the organization, changing permissions, deleting content, making payments, and actions that go beyond what the user asked for. Each automatic approval covers only the exact action that was reviewed. If a review fails or times out, the action goes to the user. Smart approvals is on for all users by default. Administrators control who can use it with custom permissions, and users can turn it off for their conversations and scheduled runs in chat options. AWS CloudTrail records each action review made through smart approvals and each change to a user's smart approvals setting. Smart approvals is available in Amazon Quick in all AWS Regions where Amazon Quick agentic capabilities are supported. For more information, see the AWS Region table . To learn more about smart approvals, see smart approvals in the Amazon Quick User Guide. For more information about Amazon Quick, see the Amazon Quick product page .

items.title: Amazon EKS Dashboard now provides fleet-wide visibility into certificate authority (CA) rotation
items.description: Today, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) announces certificate authority (CA) rotation visibility in the Amazon EKS Dashboard, giving you a consolidated view of CA rotation across your clusters. The Amazon EKS Dashboard already provides centralized visibility into your clusters across AWS Regions and accounts, and it now includes CA rotation, so you can see where action is needed without checking each cluster individually. Each Amazon EKS cluster has its own CA, and clusters created since 2018 have CAs with a 10-year validity period that are now approaching the point where rotation activities should begin. In the EKS Dashboard, you can now see your clusters and their CA rotation status, which clusters have CAs approaching expiration, and upcoming automated rotation events, so platform teams who operate many clusters can prioritize action across their fleet from one place. The Amazon EKS Dashboard aggregates data across your accounts and Regions through AWS Organizations, so you enable trusted access for the dashboard in your organization’s management account to use this capability. You view the dashboard from the US East region (us-east-1), and it is available at no additional cost. CA rotation support extends to all commercial AWS Regions, and the dashboard brings that rotation status together in one fleet-wide view. To learn more, see the Amazon EKS documentation .

items.title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances adds cross-instance and Spot consolidation
items.description: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available. Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. Until now, optimization evaluated each instance in isolation for replacement, which worked well when a capacity provider was configured with diverse instance types. However, when a capacity provider was configured with a narrow range of instance types, there were fewer opportunities to consolidate multiple underutilized instances, because no single replacement could yield savings. With cross-instance consolidation, ECS now evaluates and repacks tasks across multiple instances simultaneously. For example, in our testing with a capacity provider configured for c9g instances with a minimum size of 4xlarge, running 261 tasks (each 1 vCPU, 1.94 GiB), cross-instance consolidation reduced the fleet from 19 instances (seven 4xlarge, seven 8xlarge, four 12xlarge, and one 24xlarge) to 13 instances (eight 4xlarge and five 8xlarge), while raising CPU utilization from 42% to 91% and memory utilization from 41% to 88%. Spot consolidation applies the same approach to Spot capacity, first verifying replacement capacity is available. With these enhancements, ECS Managed Instances delivers deeper cost optimization for both your On-Demand and Spot workloads. Cross-instance and Spot consolidation are now available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions, and apply automatically to all existing and new ECS Managed Instances capacity providers. To learn more, see our documentation .

items.title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
items.description: AWS Lambda announces the Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter plugin for Lambda durable functions. This new observability plugin captures the step-by-step history of your durable executions and sends them to one or more destinations of your choice. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language. Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. Destinations include Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 for Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon OpenSearch Service. You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a sampling rate to control data volume. With the MCP server, an on-call engineer can ask an AI agent to list recent failed executions and find the cause of a failure, and a business analyst can find all transactions for a specific customer. The exporter is available for TypeScript, Python, Java, and Go. To get started, install the exporter, register the plugin in your function handler, then add the MCP server to your agent. The Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter is available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions that support Lambda durable functions. To learn more, see the Durable Execution SDK documentation and the blog post .

items.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports Kubernetes Gateway API
items.description: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API, giving customers a standard, portable way to define how traffic reaches their applications. Customers can configure application load balancing using Gateway and HTTPRoute resources, and EKS Auto Mode provisions and manages the underlying AWS infrastructure automatically. With this launch, EKS Auto Mode customers can adopt the next-generation Kubernetes traffic management standard without installing or configuring a separate controller. Capabilities include HTTP and gRPC routing, cross-namespace traffic routing for multi-team environments, weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, and automatic TLS certificate discovery through AWS Certificate Manager. Existing workloads using Ingress resources continue to work alongside Gateway API resources. To get started, see the Amazon EKS documentation . Gateway API support is included as part of EKS Auto Mode and is available in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is supported. Standard charges apply for the AWS load balancing resources provisioned.

items.title: AWS Backup adds restore testing support for Amazon Redshift
items.description: AWS Backup restore testing now supports Amazon Redshift. Restore testing helps you automate and periodically run restore tests of your backups, so you can confirm that your Amazon Redshift backups restore successfully and measure how long the restores take. You can now include Amazon Redshift in your restore testing plans alongside other supported AWS resources across storage, compute, and database services. Restore testing plans automatically select recovery points, run restores on a schedule, and measure restore job completion time against your recovery time objectives (RTO). This helps you evaluate recovery readiness and meet regulatory and compliance requirements for disaster recovery and business continuity. To get started, create a restore testing plan and assign your Amazon Redshift resources by Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or tag. Choose whether each test restores the latest or a random eligible recovery point. Optionally, use restore testing validation to confirm the restored resource before AWS Backup deletes the test resources. This support is available in all AWS Regions where both restore testing and Amazon Redshift are supported by AWS Backup. You can use the AWS Backup console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs. For a complete list of supported Regions and features, visit the AWS Backup documentation . To learn more about restore testing, visit the product page and pricing page .

items.title: Announcing the AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business unified storefront
items.description: Today, AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business announced the unified storefront. Organizations can now give their teams one curated catalog that puts software, data, and AI tools from AWS Marketplace alongside physical goods and supplies from Amazon Business. Many enterprises already buy from both, but they manage two catalogs with duplicated approval rules and separate reporting. The unified storefront can now give procurement teams one front door for both. Built on AWS Marketplace Storefront, the unified storefront lets administrators connect their organization's Amazon Business account and import Amazon Business products into their branded storefront. Administrators set governance rules once, and they apply across both catalogs. Buyers can browse AWS Marketplace listings and Amazon Business products in one place. Purchases of AWS Marketplace listings complete directly in the storefront and appear on the customer's AWS invoice. When a buyer selects an Amazon Business product, single sign-on takes them to an authenticated Amazon Business cart, so they don't need a second login. Each storefront connects only to the accounts its administrator sets up. The Amazon Business connector is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace operates to AWS Marketplace Storefront customers who have access to both the AWS Marketplace and Amazon Business APIs. To learn more, visit the AWS Marketplace Storefront product page and the AWS Marketplace Storefront User Guide .

items.title: AWS Agent Registry is now available in four additional AWS Regions
items.description: AWS Agent Registry, available through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is now available in four additional AWS Regions: Europe (London) eu-west-2, Europe (Frankfurt) eu-central-1, US East (Ohio) us-east-2, and Canada (Central) ca-central-1. AWS Agent Registry is a fully managed discovery service that provides a centralized catalog for organizing, curating, and discovering resources across your organization. With AWS Agent Registry, you can publish MCP servers, tools, agents, agent skills, and custom resources into a searchable registry, control access through an approval workflow, and enable both human users and AI agents to discover the right tools and agents through hybrid search, catalog browsing, and a native MCP endpoint. AWS Agent Registry is now available in nine AWS Regions. For a complete list of Region availability, see the AWS Regional Services List. To get started, see the AWS Agent Registry documentation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/registry.html

items.title: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now supports change notifications through Amazon EventBridge
items.description: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now delivers real-time events to Amazon EventBridge when users, groups, or group memberships or the identity store itself is created, updated, or deleted. AWS IAM Identity Center Identity Store is a central repository that allows you to manage identities and access across AWS accounts and applications, serving as the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center. This new capability helps you automatically respond to identity lifecycle events and support your security and compliance processes by detecting changes as they happen. With Identity Store change notifications, you can build automated workflows that respond to identity changes in your organization. For example, security teams can create EventBridge rules that trigger AWS Lambda functions to audit user provisioning activity, send alerts to security information and event management (SIEM) systems, or update access in downstream applications when users or groups change. Organizations that manage large workforces can also use this data to automate onboarding and offboarding when users are added to or removed from specific groups. Change notifications are available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available, and events are sent in each enabled Region of your instance. For the list of Regions, see AWS capabilities by Regions . Change notifications are available at no additional cost beyond standard Amazon EventBridge usage charges. To learn more, see Event notifications in the AWS IAM Identity Center User Guide and Identity Store events in the Amazon EventBridge Events Reference.

items.title: Amazon ECS now supports GPU sharing with NVIDIA Multi-Process Service (MPS)
items.description: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now supports GPU sharing with NVIDIA Multi-Process Service (MPS), enabling you to run multiple Amazon ECS tasks concurrently on a single NVIDIA GPU. GPU sharing helps you increase GPU utilization and reduce infrastructure costs for workloads that use only part of a GPU's capacity, such as small-model inference, AV/ADAS simulations, embedding generation, and multi-model serving. With GPU sharing, you can pack more workloads onto each GPU instance without changing your application code. You define the GPU memory each container needs and can optionally set a maximum share of GPU compute, and Amazon ECS places tasks on GPUs with available capacity as your services scale and deploy. GPU sharing is supported on Amazon ECS Managed Instances and Amazon ECS on Amazon EC2. On Amazon ECS Managed Instances, Amazon ECS also monitors the MPS control daemon that enables sharing on each instance. If the daemon stops or becomes unhealthy, Amazon ECS automatically replaces the instance and moves your tasks to healthy capacity, so your GPU workloads keep running without manual intervention. To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, AWS CloudFormation, or other infrastructure-as-code tools to create a capacity provider with NVIDIA GPU instances, set the GPU sharing strategy and memory in the container definition of your task definition, and create a service on that capacity provider. This capability is available in all AWS commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions . To learn more, visit the Amazon ECS GPU sharing documentation .

items.title: SageMaker MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16
items.description: Amazon SageMaker AI MLflow Apps now support MLflow 3.16, bringing a redesigned tracing experience and faster experiment tracking to your generative AI and machine learning workflows. MLflow 3.16 improves debugging and analysis of generative AI applications and agents. The redesigned trace explorer is now the default, with adjustable row height, reorderable columns, custom columns from any trace tag or metadata field. This release also accelerates metric charts for experiments with large metric histories. New MLflow Apps are created on MLflow 3.16 by default. Existing MLflow Apps will be upgraded to MLflow 3.16 during an upcoming maintenance window, with no action required. MLflow 3.16 is available in all AWS Regions where MLflow Apps are available. To learn more, visit the SageMaker AI MLflow developer guide .

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer supports inline attachment previews
items.description: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents preview attachments directly in the agent workspace, reducing contact handling time and limiting the need to download sensitive customer information. Agents can preview PDFs, images, and text files across email, chat, and cases, navigate between attachments, and view multi-page documents without leaving the conversation. Amazon Connect Customer attachment previews is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London) regions . To learn more and get started, please refer to the help documentation or visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports up to 384 ACUs
items.description: Amazon Aurora serverless now supports database capacity of up to 384 Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs) for Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, a 50% increase from the previous maximum of 256 ACUs. Each ACU provides approximately 2 gibibytes (GiB) of memory with corresponding CPU and networking, so a single Aurora serverless database can now scale up to 768 GiB of memory. When the workload completes, Aurora serverless automatically scales down to zero. This makes Aurora serverless especially well-suited for agentic AI applications, which typically have bursts of activity, long idle windows, and unpredictable traffic patterns. Aurora serverless handles all of it automatically, scaling capacity with your agents, so you only pay for what you use. With 384 ACU support, customers can now use Aurora serverless for even more demanding workloads while continuing to scale down to zero when not in use, paying only for the capacity consumed. For new clusters, select a supported Aurora PostgreSQL engine version and set your maximum capacity up to 384 ACUs. For existing clusters on Platform Version 4, simply modify the cluster to update the maximum capacity setting (and the engine version if needed). There will be no downtime if your database is already on Platform Version 4. For existing clusters on older platform versions, upgrade to Platform Version 4 through a pending maintenance action. 384 ACU support is available for Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23, running on Platform Version 4. To learn more, see Aurora serverless capacity in the Amazon Aurora User Guide. For pricing details and Region availability, visit Amazon Aurora Pricing .  To get started, create or modify an Aurora serverless database in the AWS Management Console .

items.title: Amazon ElastiCache expands data tiering to R8gd and R7gd nodes in Europe (Spain) and Asia Pacific (Hyderabad)
items.description: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey data tiering is now available on Graviton4-based R8gd nodes in the AWS Europe (Spain) Region, and on Graviton3-based R7gd nodes in the Europe (Spain) and Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) Regions. Data tiering is a lower-cost way to scale your Valkey clusters to hundreds of terabytes of capacity. It uses solid state drives (SSDs) on each node alongside memory. When memory fills up, ElastiCache automatically moves the least recently used items to SSD. When your application reads an item stored on SSD, ElastiCache moves it back into memory before serving the request. Data tiering is a good fit for workloads that regularly access up to 20% of their dataset, and for applications that can tolerate some extra latency when they read data from SSD. R8gd nodes are powered by AWS Graviton4 processors. They deliver up to 47% higher throughput, up to 43% lower P99 latency, and up to 31% better price-performance than Graviton3-based nodes of the same size. R7gd nodes are powered by AWS Graviton3 processors. They deliver up to 28% more throughput (read and write operations per second), up to 21% better P99 latency, and up to 25% more network bandwidth than Graviton2-based nodes. Actual performance varies by node size and workload. You can use data tiering on R8gd and R7gd nodes with Valkey 7.2 and later. To get started, create a new cluster or upgrade an existing one with the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, or the AWS SDKs. For pricing, see the   Amazon ElastiCache pricing page  . To learn more, see   Data tiering  and   Supported node types  in the ElastiCache documentation.

items.title: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now supports changing durability on existing clusters
items.description: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now lets you enable or disable durability on your existing node-based clusters. Previously, you couldn't change the durability configuration of an existing cluster in place. This made it harder to move from caching to persistent data store use cases, or to adapt as your application requirements change. Now you can change durability at any point in your application's lifecycle. You can choose between two durability options: synchronous and asynchronous writes. Synchronous writes persist data across at least two AZs before responding to the client, designed for zero data loss at single-digit millisecond write latency. Asynchronous writes persist data after responding to the client, maintaining microsecond write latency at no additional cost. However, up to 10 seconds of uncommitted data could be lost in the rare event of a failure. Both options maintain microsecond read latency. You can now use ElastiCache for a broader set of use cases beyond caching where data loss is unacceptable such as AI agent long-term memory, AI agent workflow state, knowledge bases for RAG applications, payment tokenization, and real-time inventory management. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where ElastiCache for Valkey 9.0 and later is available. To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS SDK, or AWS CLI. For pricing, see the   Amazon ElastiCache pricing page . To learn more, see   Durability  in the ElastiCache documentation.

Corretto 27.0.1.0.11, 25.0.5.0.10, 21.0.13.0.11, 17.0.21.0.11, 11.0.33.0.10, and 8u512 are now available for download . items.title: Amazon Neptune now supports online index rebuild to reclaim storage
items.description: Amazon Neptune Database now supports online index rebuild, a new capability that helps database administrators and application teams defragment Neptune indexes and reclaim unused storage space without taking their database offline. Over time, insert, update, and delete operations create gaps of unused space within data pages, keeping the VolumeBytesUsed metric artificially elevated even after data is deleted. This fragmentation increases I/O costs and degrades query performance for teams running Gremlin, openCypher, or SPARQL workloads at scale. With online index rebuild, read and write queries continue uninterrupted on both the writer instance and read replicas throughout the entire rebuild process. You can target all indexes, only quad indexes, or only dictionary indexes, making this feature well-suited for post-deletion cleanup, periodic maintenance, storage limit management, and performance tuning on heavily fragmented databases. Tunable concurrency and write buffer size settings let you balance rebuild speed against workload impact, while built-in storage safety mechanisms protect against storage exhaustion during the operation. Online index rebuild is available starting with Amazon Neptune engine release 1.5.0.0 on provisioned writer instances, in all regions where Amazon Neptune Database is supported. To learn more about configuring and running online index rebuild, including API references and tuning guidance, visit the Amazon Neptune documentation .

items.title: Amazon Bedrock now offers Canada cross-Region inference for Claude Haiku 5.5
items.description: Amazon Bedrock now offers Canada cross-Region inference (CRIS) for Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5. Customers with strict data residency requirements can now keep inference processing entirely within Canada. Canada CRIS routes requests only between ca-central-1 (Canada Central) and ca-west-1 (Canada West, Calgary). This helps organizations in financial services, healthcare, the public sector, and other regulated industries meet federal and provincial data residency requirements. Canada CRIS adds to the inference options already available to customers in Canada. US CRIS and global CRIS remain fully supported for Claude Haiku 5.5. Both route requests across a broader set of AWS Regions, and global CRIS also offers cost savings, which makes these options a good fit for workloads that don't require inference processing to stay in Canada. Canada CRIS is designated as an inference profile with limited model selection. Future models and model versions might not be released for this profile. We recommend Canada CRIS for workloads that must keep inference processing within Canada. For more details, see Inference profiles with limited model selection in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. For the most current information about model availability in each Region, see Regional availability by models in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. To get started with Claude models on Amazon Bedrock, visit the Amazon Bedrock console.

items.title: Amazon ECR now supports replication backfill for existing container images
items.description: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replication backfill, enabling you to replicate existing images in your private registry to your configured replication registry destinations. Previously, replication only applied to images pushed after the replication configuration was enabled, requiring customers to manually retag images to trigger replication of preexisting images. With replication backfill, you can now replicate your full image catalog to new or existing destinations with a single API call. Replication backfill is useful when expanding to a new AWS Region, validating disaster recovery readiness, updating replication rules, or ensuring complete image catalogs exist across Regions for compliance purposes. You can run up to ten backfill jobs concurrently, monitor progress and per-image results through new APIs, and stop a job at any time without deleting images that have already been replicated. Replication backfill is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECR is available. To learn more, refer to the Amazon ECR user guide .
